newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish govt borrows PLN 1 bln from c.bank-finmin.
newsitem.headline: Polish govt borrows PLN 1 bln from c.bank-finmin.

text.p: The Polish government borrowed one billion zlotys for flood relief purposes from the National Bank of Poland (NBP) last Saturday, Finance Minister Marek Belka told a news briefing on Tuesday.
"The first tranche of the NBP credit was taken on Saturady and amounted to one billion zlotys," Belka said.
Asked what interest the government would have to pay Belka said the loan was "at market rates" but declined to be more specific.

Last week parliament passed a budget law amendment allowing the government to borrow an additional 2.5 billion zlotys from the central bank for flood relief on top of this year's original limit of the same size which has already been used up.
Andrzej Pilat, head of the government's flood relief office, said last week that the government had already borrowed 3.5 billion zlotys for the purpose outside of the NBP credit.

Economists have blasted the government's latest method of cash-raising, saying borrowing more from the central bank was the worst possible scenario from the point of view of inflation as it meant printing money.
The central bank has said it would start gathering deposits on the market to try and offset the inflationary impact of the loan of the loan.
Torrential rain in southern Poland this month has caused floods which have killed at least 36 people and forced tens of thousands out of their homes.
